fairness_notes: Both solvers single-threaded: Fortran -np 1 -nt 1 (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1); pyradioss one NumPy process (CLI -nt not passed).

TIMING PROVENANCE (M38 change): every record carries timing_source. PORT records are FRESH M38 wall clocks measured around each pyradioss subprocess. FORTRAN records are CARRIED from perf_m37.json unchanged. Rationale: the four M38 fix-packs are all PORT changes (tetra4 volume-sign, /PROP pack incl. SH_ORTH fabric + spring_general, LAW70 hourglass, energy-ledger + hardening); the Fortran solver, binaries and decks are unchanged since M37 and run single-process DETERMINISTICALLY (empirically: c01 Fortran re-run reproduced M37's FRAMET01.csv byte-identically, md5 3a5c5bbbe793, max cell diff 0.0). Re-running Fortran would only re-measure a deterministic control under the live user MPI job (worse data) and steal ~133 min of CPU from that job.
starter_s/engine_s are subprocess WALL CLOCKS (include process startup); *_self_s are the solvers' own reported ELAPSED TIME from their .out listings.
Same machine as perf_m36/m37 (13th Gen i9-13900H, 20 logical processors); background load uncontrolled (desktop).
n_cycles differs per solver on the same deck (independent time-step evolution); elements_x_cycles_per_s is the fairer cross-solver rate.

Official case ids c00..c51 are IDENTICAL to perf_m37.json (the case set is built by importing the M37 driver's build_cases()); c40+ are the M37-unlocked packages (RD-E-1000 BT, RD-V-0220 LAW70 foam, RD-V-0230 LAW19 fabric).
SKIPPED-SLOW rows carry the PARTIAL port timings up to the 900 s budget, not a completed run.

CPU CONTENTION (M38): the user's own 12-13-process MPI job (engine_win64_impi.exe) was live on this box for the whole M38 port sweep. Each case's port run is tasklist-sampled at start and end (impi_procs recorded in parity_m38); a port record flagged contended (contention_note) has an UPPER-BOUND wall clock, not a clean measurement. Parity classes and cycle counts are UNAFFECTED. Fortran (M37-carried) records keep M37's own contention flag.

F/P wall-clock RATIOS in the timing table mix a FRESH-M38 port clock with an M37 Fortran clock measured under different load — they are indicative of order-of-magnitude only, not a same-run head-to-head.
